references.text: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus gives a parallel exhortation to reconcile with one's opponent while still on the way, otherwise one may be thrown into prison: "You will certainly not come out of there until you have paid the last penny" ([ref:Matt 5:25-26|Matthew 5:25-26]). This is the closest parallel to Luke 12:59 and uses almost identical wording about paying down to the last coin.

In the parable of the unforgiving servant, the one who does not forgive is handed over to the jailers "until he had paid back everything he owed" ([ref:Matt 18:34-35|Matthew 18:34-35]). The same principle as in Luke 12:59: the debt must be fully settled, and there is no way out until everything has been paid.

The preceding verses in context ([ref:Luk 12:57-58|Luke 12:57-58]) establish the situation to which verse 59 is the conclusion: Jesus urges making peace with one's opponent on the way to the judge, to avoid the severe judgment described in verse 59.

Proverbs gives a parallel wisdom exhortation: "Do not rush to court with anyone. For what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame? Settle your case with your neighbor, but do not reveal another's secret" ([ref:Ordsp 25:8-10|Proverbs 25:8-10]). As in Luke 12:59, the advice is to resolve disputes before they escalate into a formal judgment.

Jesus says that people will have to give an account for every careless word they speak on the day of judgment ([ref:Matt 12:36|Matthew 12:36]). This underscores the same principle of complete settlement as in Luke 12:59 – no detail will be overlooked in God's judgment.
